hidden_items.why: Local site 2 (the downcallHandle statement). java.lang.foreign.Linker is an INTERFACE, so the body that runs is chosen from the run-time class of `linker`, which is bound at local site 1 - a DIFFERENT local site that s0.7 excludes from what is local here - and downcallHandle itself has two overloads that differ materially (the two-argument form has no address and produces a handle taking one). hidden_items.checklist_item: H3 - Overload or dynamic dispatch not locally evident
hidden_items.why: Local site 3 (`int magnitude = (int) abs.invokeExact(-3);`). `invokeExact` is signature-polymorphic (JLS SE26 15.12.3): the code that actually runs is whatever target the MethodHandle in `abs` holds, and `abs` is bound at local site 2, which s0.7 excludes from this site. The set of bodies compatible with this site is therefore every method handle target in the program - far more than two - and nothing here narrows it.

hidden_items.checklist_item: H7 - Implicit representation change
hidden_items.why: Local site 3. The Java int argument is marshalled into the C ABI's 32-bit integer and the C result back into a Java int, per a FunctionDescriptor bound at a DIFFERENT local site. Nothing at this site names a layout, a byte order or a marshalling step: the only token that looks like one, `(int)`, is the JLS 15.12.3 call-site return-type ascription, not the ABI conversion. The change is FFI layout, which H7 names explicitly as observable, so the 'fully unobservable' exclusion does not apply, and it is not written at the local site, so the explicit-conversion exclusion does not apply.

hidden_items.checklist_item: H9 - Hidden side effects on existing state
hidden_items.why: Local site 3, a distinct rule. Executing the handle transfers control out of the JVM into foreign code, which may read or write arbitrary process state - the behaviour Linker's restricted-method clause warns about - and Java has no token at all for that crossing: no `unsafe`, no `extern`, no effect annotation. The only signal the frozen toolchain produces is a RUN-TIME warning on stderr, which s0.7 does not count as a local signal. A different normative statement from H7's marshalling rule, imposing a different reader obligation, hence a distinct event under s1.3.2.
